name: Fhir Ontology Autocomplete Module
description: This module provides support for referencing an external Fhir based ontology server to lookup values.

system-settings.name: The FHIR server url to use. eg. https://tx.ontoserver.csiro.au/fhir or https://snowstorm-fhir.snomedtools.org/fhir. Don't leave a trailing slash.

Maximum number of seconds to wait to connect to the FHIR server before giving up. Protects against an unreachable or refusing host; it does not currently bound a server that accepts the connection and then stalls. Leave blank to use the default of 10 seconds.
Does the FHIR server support implicit SNOMEDCT valuesets?
Does the FHIR server support implicit LOINC valuesets?

The fhir server may require some form of authentication, currently OAuth2 Client Credentials and Basic Auth is supported. Communication with the FHIR server is made by the redcap server, not the users browser.

action-tags.description:
@FHIR-ONTOLOGY-HIDECHOICE='code1,code2'
For a field using this module's FHIR ontology support, hides the listed codes so they never appear as selectable options in the field's autocomplete search. Codes are a comma-separated list, matched against the FHIR code only - not the code system, so a code shared by two systems in the same ValueSet cannot be hidden selectively.
This module also recognizes the older @HIDECHOICE tag name for the same purpose (for backward compatibility with existing fields); it isn't listed separately here because it collides with REDCap's own built-in @HIDECHOICE tag for standard choice fields, which this popup always shows instead.

@FHIR-ONTOLOGY-OPTIONS='option1;option2;...'
For a field using this module's FHIR ontology support, controls how the field's autocomplete search behaves. Semicolon-separated options (not comma-separated, since priority-codes needs its own comma-separated code list):
  • return-all - drop the server-side text filter and rank matches locally instead. Intended only for small, fully-enumerated ValueSets (e.g. a short answer list) - it still only fetches up to the field's result limit (20 by default) with no filter, so any entry beyond that limit in the server's own ordering is silently unreachable regardless of match quality; setting it on a large ValueSet (SNOMED CT, etc.) is also slow and wasteful, since the unfiltered request repeats on every search keystroke.
  • code-template=${CODE} (or ${SYSTEM}) - overrides the format of the value stored for this field (default ${CODE}|${SYSTEM}). Only use a code-only template when the field's ValueSet is known to use a single code system - see this module's README for the collision risk otherwise.
  • priority-codes=code1,code2 - sorts these FHIR codes to the top of search results whenever they appear, in the order listed.
Example: @FHIR-ONTOLOGY-OPTIONS='return-all;code-template=${CODE}'
